# Week 04 Cheat Sheet: Threats in the Modern World - II **Course:** Biodiversity for Sustainability **Instructor:** Dr. Ankur Awadhiya, IFS **Lectures Covered:** Lecture 16 to Lecture 20 **Quizzes Cross-Referenced:** `quiz_week_4.txt` ($N=10$) & `quiz_week_0.txt` (Practice) --- ## 1. High-Yield Terminological & Definitional Matrix | Citation | Term / Concept | Operational Scientific Definition | Exam Archetype | Exam Question Tag | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | `[Lec 16]` | **Classical Climate Period (WMO)** | The standard baseline period of **30 consecutive years** used by the World Meteorological Organization (WMO) to calculate statistical climatic normals and averages. | Numerical Baseline | `[TESTED - 30% REPEAT POOL]` (W4-Q2) | | `[Lec 16]` | **Shelford’s Law of Tolerance** | Ecological principle stating that organism abundance and distribution are determined by a bell-shaped tolerance curve across environmental factors; population reaches zero at lethal extremes. | Graphic / Law | `[TESTED - 30% REPEAT POOL]` (W4-Q4) | | `[Lec 16]` | **Major Climatic Changes Set** | The four primary interconnected global climatic alterations: (1) Rising temperatures, (2) Changing rainfall patterns, (3) More frequent extreme weather events, and (4) Shifting biological seasons. | Criteria Set | `[TESTED - 30% REPEAT POOL]` (W4-Q6) | | `[Lec 16]` | **Specialist Climate Vulnerability** | Specialist species decline earliest because they possess narrow physiological and ecological tolerances and lack alternative diet, habitat, or thermal options. | Mechanistic Rationale | `[TESTED - 30% REPEAT POOL]` (W4-Q3) | | `[Lec 16]` | **Phenological Mismatch** | Asynchrony caused when climate warming shifts the seasonal timing of interacting species at unequal rates (e.g., insect emergence desynchronizing from migratory bird chick hatching). | Temporal Disruption | `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]` | | `[Lec 17]` | **Ocean Acidification** | The reduction in oceanic pH driven by the absorption of excess atmospheric anthropogenic carbon dioxide ($CO_2$), depleting seawater carbonate ions ($CO_3^{2-}$). | Chemical Process | `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]` | | `[Lec 17]` | **Eutrophication** | Rapid, excessive algal and phytoplankton proliferation triggered by agricultural and domestic nutrient runoff (Nitrogen and Phosphorus), causing oxygen depletion and aquatic dead zones. | Causal Mechanism | `[TESTED - 30% REPEAT POOL]` (W4-Q8) | | `[Lec 17]` | **Desertification** | Biological and physical degradation of dryland ecosystems resulting from human exploitation (overgrazing, deforestation, poor irrigation) compounded by climatic variations. | Land Degradation | `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]` | | `[Lec 17]` | **Phosphorus Cycle Anomaly** | The fundamental biogeochemical distinction: unlike the carbon, nitrogen, and hydrological cycles, the phosphorus cycle has **no major atmospheric gaseous reservoir**. | Chemical Comparison | `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]` | | `[Lec 17]` | **Decomposers' Ecological Role** | Heterotrophic organisms (bacteria, fungi, detritivores) that break down dead organic biomass and metabolic wastes, recycling locked elements back into the abiotic nutrient pool. | Functional Role | `[TESTED - 30% REPEAT POOL]` (W4-Q10) | | `[Lec 18]` | **Overexploitation (Awadhiya Formulation)** | Harvesting or extracting biological organisms and forest resources faster than natural reproduction and recruitment can replace them. | Forward Definition | `[TESTED - 30% REPEAT POOL]` (W4-Q1) | | `[Lec 18]` | **IUCN Extinct in the Wild (EW)** | Red List status assigned to a species that no longer possesses wild free-ranging populations and survives exclusively in captivity, zoos, botanical gardens, or seed banks. | Framework Category | `[TESTED - 30% REPEAT POOL]` (W4-Q5) | | `[Lec 18]` | **Functional Extinction** | A state where a tiny population remains alive (e.g., only two post-reproductive females), but can no longer reproduce, sustain genetic diversity, or perform its ecological role. | Reverse Definition | `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]` | | `[Lec 18]` | **Chytridiomycosis** | Epidemic fungal infection caused by *Batrachochytrium dendrobatidis* (Bd); disrupts amphibian cutaneous respiration and electrolyte transport, causing $>90$ species extinctions globally. | Infectious Disease | `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]` | | `[Lec 19]` | **Allee Effect** | A positive density-dependent phenomenon where individual biological fitness, group foraging efficiency, or per-capita reproductive success fails when population density falls below a critical threshold. | Population Dynamic | `[TESTED - 30% REPEAT POOL]` (W4-Q9) | | `[Lec 19]` | **Genetic Rescue** | Deliberate introduction of unrelated, genetically diverse individuals from an outside population into an inbred, declining population to restore heterozygosity and reduce deleterious defects. | Applied Genetics | `[TESTED - 30% REPEAT POOL]` (W4-Q7) | | `[Lec 19]` | **Extinction Vortex** | A self-reinforcing downward spiral where small population size triggers inbreeding and genetic drift, causing lower fitness, higher mortality, and even smaller population size. | System Feedback | `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]` | | `[Lec 19]` | **Demographic Stochasticity** | Random chance fluctuations in births, deaths, litter sizes, or sex ratios that disproportionately threaten small, isolated populations with sudden extinction. | Statistical Risk | `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]` | | `[Lec 19]` | **Genetic Swamping (Pollution)** | Deleterious hybridization where rare wild populations interbreed with abundant domestic, feral, or exotic relatives, erasing locally adapted genotypes. | Genetic Threat | `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]` | | `[Lec 20]` | **Sixth Mass Extinction (Anthropocene)** | The ongoing global extinction crisis driven by human overexploitation, habitat destruction, pollution, and climate change; distinguished by occurring orders of magnitude faster than historical background rates. | Macro-Evolutionary | `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]` | --- ## 2. Shelford's Law of Tolerance & Ecological Zones ```mermaid flowchart LR Z1["Lethal Zone (Left Extreme)
Population = 0 [Lec 16]"] --- Z2["Stress Zone (Sub-Optimal)
Low Population Abundance [Lec 16]"] Z2 --- Z3["Optimum Zone (Center)
Peak Population & Fitness [Lec 16]"] Z3 --- Z4["Stress Zone (Sub-Optimal)
Low Population Abundance [Lec 16]"] Z4 --- Z5["Lethal Zone (Right Extreme)
Population = 0 [Lec 16]"] ``` * `[Lec 16]` **Optimum Center (Green):** Optimal thermal/moisture conditions where metabolic efficiency is maximized; supports high reproductive output, competitive dominance, and peak population density `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]`. * `[Lec 16]` **Zones of Physiological Stress (Yellow):** Flanking sub-optimal conditions; organism survives with elevated metabolic expenditure, but exhibits stunted growth, suppressed reproduction, and declining abundance `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]`. * `[Lec 16]` **Lethal Limits of Intolerance (Red):** Environmental conditions exceed physiological coping mechanisms entirely; **the population drops to zero** `[TESTED - 30% REPEAT POOL]` (W4-Q4). * `[Lec 16]` **Simultaneous Constraint Rule:** Organisms do not face single isolated variables; survival requires fitting within the optimum/tolerable zones across multiple physical gradients simultaneously (temperature, moisture, salinity, pH) `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]`. --- ## 3. Biogeochemical Cycles: Comparative Metabolic Matrix | Citation | Biogeochemical Cycle | Primary Natural Reservoirs | Key Biological / Geochemical Processes | Anthropogenic Perturbation & Ecological Consequence | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | `[Lec 17]` | **Carbon Cycle ($C$)** | Ocean waters, sedimentary rocks, fossil fuels, terrestrial vegetation, atmosphere. | Photosynthesis captures atmospheric $CO_2$; respiration, microbial decomposition, and combustion return $CO_2$ to air; ocean-atmosphere gas exchange. | Fossil fuel burning and deforestation accelerate active cycling $\rightarrow$ Greenhouse warming and severe ocean acidification `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]`. | | `[Lec 17]` | **Nitrogen Cycle ($N$)** | Atmosphere ($78\%$ as inert $N_2$ gas), soil organic matter, living biomass. | Biological nitrogen fixation (Rhizobium, cyanobacteria), ammonification, nitrification ($NO_2^-, NO_3^-$), and bacterial denitrification. | Haber-Bosch industrial synthesis and massive synthetic fertilizer runoff $\rightarrow$ Atmospheric emissions and severe aquatic eutrophication `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]`. | | `[Lec 17]` | **Phosphorus Cycle ($P$)** | Sedimentary rocks, marine sediments, soils (NO atmospheric gas phase!). | Weathering of phosphate minerals, plant uptake from soil water, trophic transfer, bacterial decomposition, long-term oceanic sedimentation. | Phosphate mining, detergent release, and agricultural runoff $\rightarrow$ Massive freshwater eutrophication and algal blooms `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]`. | | `[Lec 17]` | **Hydrological Cycle ($H_2O$)** | Oceans ($97\%$), cryosphere glaciers/ice caps, groundwater, surface water, atmosphere. | Evaporation, evapotranspiration, atmospheric condensation, precipitation, surface runoff, soil infiltration, and groundwater percolation. | Deforestation reduces transpiration, increasing surface flash runoff; land clearing and climate change accelerate dryland desertification `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]`. | --- ## 4. Empirical Biological Entities, Scientific Binomials & Regional Taxa | Citation | Common Name / Case Study | Scientific Name / Taxonomic Group | Geographic Region / Site | Tested Ecological Mechanism, Vulnerability & Conservation Status | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | `[Lec 16]` | **Coral Reef Ecosystems** | Class Anthozoa (Scleractinian Corals) | Tropical Shallow Oceans | Ocean Acidification Vulnerability: Lower seawater pH reduces available carbonate ions ($CO_3^{2-}$); inhibits calcium carbonate ($CaCO_3$) aragonite skeleton deposition `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]`. | | `[Lec 18]` | **Northern White Rhinoceros** | *Ceratotherium simum cottoni* | Ol Pejeta Conservancy, Kenya | Functional Extinction archetype: Only 2 living individuals remain on Earth, both females (Najin and Fatu); natural breeding is biologically impossible `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]`. | | `[Lec 18]` | **Great Indian Bustard (GIB)** | *Ardeotis nigriceps* (Otididae) | Desert National Park, Thar Desert, Rajasthan (India) | Critically Endangered (CR) heavy-bodied bird; poor frontal vision prevents avoiding overhead high-voltage power lines; low fecundity (1 egg/year) prevents population recovery `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]`. | | `[Lec 18]` | **Javan & Sumatran Rhinoceros** | *Rhinoceros sondaicus* & *Dicerorhinus sumatrensis* | Southeast Asian Rain Forests (Java & Sumatra) | Critically Endangered (CR): Extreme population crashes; fewer than 80 wild individuals survive in fragmented jungle reserves `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]`. | | `[Lec 18]` | **Laysan Albatross Chicks** | *Phoebastria immutabilis* | Midway Atoll, Pacific Ocean | Marine Plastic Pollution: Pelagic parents mistake floating surface plastic debris for squid/fish; chicks starve to death with stomachs impacted with plastic `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]`. | | `[Lec 19]` | **Dodo** *(Flightless insular bird)* | *Raphus cucullatus* (Columbidae) | Mauritius (Indian Ocean, east of Madagascar) | Extinct (EX) archetype: Giant flightless dove (~1 m tall); lacked evolutionary fear of predators; ground nests destroyed by sailors and introduced pigs, monkeys, rats within $<100$ years `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]`. | | `[Lec 19]` | **Asiatic Wild Dog / Dhole** | *Cuon alpinus* (Canidae) | Indian Forest Landscapes | Allee Effect archetype: Obligate cooperative pack hunters; hunting success relies on coordinated packs exhausting ungulate prey; pack decline below threshold causes hunting failure and starvation `[TESTED - 30% REPEAT POOL]` (W4-Q9). | | `[Lec 19]` | **Florida Panther Genetic Rescue** | *Puma concolor coryi* | South Florida Swamps (USA) | Genetic Rescue archetype: Population crashed to ~30 in 1990s; inbreeding caused kinked tails, atrial septal heart defects, and cryptorchidism; 8 Texas cougars (*P. c. stanleyana*) introduced in 1995 rebounded population to $>200$ `[TESTED - 30% REPEAT POOL]` (W4-Q7). | --- ## 5. IUCN Red List Categories Hierarchy (Lecture 18) ```mermaid flowchart TD ALL["All Evaluated Species"] --> EX["1. Extinct (EX): No living individuals anywhere [Lec 18]"] ALL --> EW["2. Extinct in the Wild (EW): Survives ONLY in captivity/seed banks [Lec 18]"] ALL --> THR["Threatened Categories"] THR --> CR["3. Critically Endangered (CR): Extremely high extinction risk [Lec 18]"] THR --> EN["4. Endangered (EN): Very high extinction risk [Lec 18]"] THR --> VU["5. Vulnerable (VU): High risk of endangerment [Lec 18]"] ALL --> NT["6. Near Threatened (NT): Close to qualifying for threatened status [Lec 18]"] ALL --> LC["7. Least Concern (LC): Abundant and widespread [Lec 18]"] ALL --> DD["8. Data Deficient (DD): Inadequate information to make assessment [Lec 18]"] ``` * `[Lec 18]` **Extinct (EX):** Comprehensive field surveys fail to locate a single living individual anywhere on Earth (e.g., Dodo *Raphus cucullatus*, Passenger Pigeon *Ectopistes migratorius*) `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]`. * `[Lec 18]` **Extinct in the Wild (EW):** Survives **only** in zoos, botanical gardens, captive breeding facilities, or seed banks; free-ranging populations completely vanished from historic geographic range `[TESTED - 30% REPEAT POOL]` (W4-Q5). * `[Lec 18]` **Critically Endangered (CR):** Facing an extremely high risk of extinction in the wild in the immediate future; evaluated by severe population reduction, tiny geographic range, or adult count $<50$ (e.g., Great Indian Bustard) `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]`. --- ## 6. The Extinction Vortex Feedback Loop (Lecture 19) ```mermaid flowchart TD P1["Small Population Size [Lec 19]"] --> P2["Inbreeding Depression & Genetic Drift [Lec 19]"] P2 --> P3["Loss of Heterozygosity & Allelic Diversity [Lec 19]"] P3 --> P4["Reduced Individual Fitness & Elevated Disease Vulnerability [Lec 19]"] P4 --> P5["Higher Mortality Rates & Reduced Fecundity [Lec 19]"] P5 --> P1 ``` * `[Lec 19]` **Vortex Mechanics:** Small populations do not decline linearly; they enter an accelerating, positive-feedback extinction spiral where internal genetic decay multiplies external ecological vulnerabilities `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]`. * `[Lec 19]` **Tripartite Stochastic Threats:** 1. *Demographic Stochasticity:* Random fluctuations in sex ratio (e.g., all remaining offspring born male) `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]`. 2. *Environmental Stochasticity:* Unpredictable annual fluctuations in rainfall, temperature, or food availability. 3. *Natural Catastrophes:* Singular severe events (cyclones, wildfires, epizootic outbreaks) wiping out remaining clusters. --- ## 7. Contrastive Pairs & Diagnostic Trap Summary * `[Lec 16]` **Climate vs. Weather Trap:** Weather is short-term atmospheric variation; Climate is the statistical distribution of weather over the **30-year classical baseline** `[TESTED - 30% REPEAT POOL]` (W4-Q2). * `[Lec 16]` **Shelford Curve Boundary Trap:** Distractors claiming that outside tolerance limits *"species immediately adapt genetically"* or *"shift to optimum range"* are false. Beyond tolerance limits, **the population drops to zero** `[TESTED - 30% REPEAT POOL]` (W4-Q4). * `[Lec 17]` **Eutrophication Nutrient Trap:** Eutrophication is driven primarily by **Nitrogen and Phosphorus**; distractors substitute carbon or heavy metals. Oxygen is NOT released; it is severely depleted by bacterial decomposition of dead algae `[TESTED - 30% REPEAT POOL]` (W4-Q8). * `[Lec 17]` **Decomposer Role Trap:** Distractors claiming decomposers *"remove producers"* or *"convert nutrients into fossil fuels"* are absurd; their role is to return elements to the abiotic nutrient pool `[TESTED - 30% REPEAT POOL]` (W4-Q10). * `[Lec 18]` **Extinct vs. Extinct in the Wild:** Extinct = zero individuals on Earth; Extinct in the Wild = survives in captive, human-managed settings `[TESTED - 30% REPEAT POOL]` (W4-Q5). * `[Lec 19]` **Allee Effect Trap:** Distractors define Allee effect as *"increased survival at high nutrients"* or *"faster adaptation"*; correct answer is strictly **fitness/reproductive failure at low density/size** `[TESTED - 30% REPEAT POOL]` (W4-Q9). * `[Lec 19]` **Genetic Rescue vs. Genetic Swamping:** * *Rescue:* Positive, scientifically guided introduction of diverse conspecifics to relieve inbreeding depression `[TESTED - 30% REPEAT POOL]` (W4-Q7). * *Swamping:* Harmful dilution of rare wild gene pools by fertile domestic or invasive relatives `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]`.

cheatsheets.title: Week 05 Cheat Sheet: Benefits of Coexistence
cheatsheets.content:
# Week 05 Cheat Sheet: Benefits of Coexistence

**Course:** Biodiversity for Sustainability 
**Instructor:** Dr. Ankur Awadhiya, IFS 
**Lectures Covered:** Lecture 21 to Lecture 25 
**Quizzes Cross-Referenced:** `quiz_week_5.txt` ($N=10$) & `quiz_week_0.txt` (Practice) 

---

## 1. High-Yield Terminological & Definitional Matrix

| Citation | Term / Concept | Operational Scientific Definition | Exam Archetype | Exam Question Tag |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `[Lec 21]` | **Fortress Conservation Limits** | The flawed assumption that biodiversity can be sustained solely by strictly isolating it within fenced reserves; fails because $>80\%$ of land is outside PAs and species must move across boundaries. | Critical Concept | `[TESTED - 30% REPEAT POOL]` (W5-Q7) |
| `[Lec 21]` | **Reserve Movement Spillover** | The ecological reality that wildlife constantly traverses protected area borders into surrounding human matrices for forage, water, mates, or seasonal migration. | Spatial Dynamic | `[TESTED - 30% REPEAT POOL]` (W5-Q2) |
| `[Lec 21]` | **Shared Landscapes (Matrix)** | Working human-dominated mosaics (agroforestry, croplands, community pastures) managed to support both local livelihoods and wildlife dispersal corridors. | Applied Management | `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]` |
| `[Lec 21]` | **Ecosystem Engineer (Keystone)** | A species (e.g., Asian Elephant) that physically creates, modifies, and maintains habitat structures, nutrient flows, and water holes essential for multiple coexisting species. | Ecological Role | `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]` |
| `[Lec 22]` | **Microclimate Regulation** | Biophysical moderation of local ambient climate by vegetation through canopy shading, lowering surface temperatures ($10\text{--}15^\circ\text{C}$), and humidifying air via evapotranspiration. | Forward Definition | `[TESTED - 30% REPEAT POOL]` (W5-Q5) |
| `[Lec 22]` | **Hydrological Soil Regulation** | The regulation of water flows by root architecture and living soil communities, increasing rainwater infiltration, recharging aquifers, and attenuating surface storm runoff. | Forward Definition | `[TESTED - 30% REPEAT POOL]` (W5-Q8) |
| `[Lec 22]` | **Biological Pest Suppression** | The regulation of agricultural herbivorous pests by natural multi-species predator assemblages (insectivorous bats, birds, parasitoid wasps, spiders) without chemical inputs. | Applied Service | `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]` |
| `[Lec 23]` | **Non-Timber Forest Products (NTFPs)** | Wild biological resources harvested from forests without felling timber: fruits, edible nuts, resins, gums, medicinal plants, bamboo, fibers, honey, and tendu leaves. | Set Classification | `[TESTED - 30% REPEAT POOL]` (W5-Q4) |
| `[Lec 23]` | **Option Value** | The economic and societal benefit of preserving biological diversity today to keep it available for unforeseen, future utilitarian applications (e.g., novel pharmaceuticals, genes). | Economic Metric | `[TESTED - 30% REPEAT POOL]` (W5-Q3) |
| `[Lec 23]` | **Total Economic Value (TEV)** | Comprehensive valuation framework encompassing all direct use, indirect use, option, bequest, and existence values of ecosystems. | Economic Framework | `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]` |
| `[Lec 23]` | **Bequest Value** | Non-use value reflecting the satisfaction or moral duty derived from ensuring that biodiversity is conserved intact for future human generations. | Forward Definition | `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]` |
| `[Lec 23]` | **Existence Value** | Non-use value derived purely from the knowledge that wild species and wilderness areas exist, independent of any present or anticipated human utilization. | Forward Definition | `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]` |
| `[Lec 24]` | **Cultural Services of Biodiversity** | Non-material ecosystem benefits: recreation, aesthetic beauty, spiritual inspiration, artistic creation, educational enrichment, cultural heritage, and shared civic spaces. | Criteria Set | `[TESTED - 30% REPEAT POOL]` (W5-Q6) |
| `[Lec 24]` | **Health Support via Ecosystems** | Protection of human physical and mental health through biological filtration of air/water pollutants, suppression of infectious zoonoses, and biophilic psychological restoration. | Applied Health | `[TESTED - 30% REPEAT POOL]` (W5-Q10) |
| `[Lec 24]` | **Ethnopharmacology & TEK** | The scientific study of indigenous medical knowledge and bioactive compounds derived from wild plants (e.g., Artemisinin from *Artemisia annua*). | Ethnobotany | `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]` |
| `[Lec 25]` | **Human-Wildlife Conflict (HWC)** | Situations where wildlife requirements or behavior clash directly with human interests, causing crop damage, livestock predation, human injury/death, fear, and retaliation. | Forward Definition | `[TESTED - 30% REPEAT POOL]` (W5-Q1) |
| `[Lec 25]` | **Inadequate Spatial Planning** | Uncoordinated construction of linear infrastructure (roads, railways, canals), urban sprawl, and farming expansion that fragments corridors and drives HWC outbreaks. | Causal Rationale | `[TESTED - 30% REPEAT POOL]` (W5-Q9) |
| `[Lec 25]` | **Coexistence Principle: Risk Reduction** | Proactive preventive management (early warning telemetry, predator-proof corrals, bio-fencing, spatial zoning) implemented before conflict incidents happen. | Management Protocol | `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]` |

---

## 2. Total Economic Value (TEV) Framework for Biodiversity

```mermaid
flowchart TD
 TEV["Total Economic Value (TEV) [Lec 23]"] --> UV["Use Values [Lec 23]"]
 TEV --> NUV["Non-Use Values [Lec 23]"]
 UV --> DUV["Direct Use: Harvested timber, fish, wild foods, ecotourism [Lec 23]"]
 UV --> IUV["Indirect Use: Watershed buffering, pollination, carbon storage [Lec 23]"]
 UV --> OV["Option Value: Preserving biodiversity for future unknown uses [Lec 23]"]
 NUV --> BV["Bequest Value: Conserving ecosystems for future generations [Lec 23]"]
 NUV --> EV["Existence Value: Intrinsic satisfaction that wild species exist [Lec 23]"]
```

* `[Lec 23]` **Direct Use Value:** Extractive goods directly harvested from ecosystems (timber, fuelwood, fish, medicinal plants) and non-extractive services (hiking, ecotourism, scientific research) `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]`.
* `[Lec 23]` **Indirect Use Value:** Functional ecological services that support human economic activity without direct physical extraction (e.g., wetland water filtration saving millions in municipal sewage treatment costs; forest carbon sequestration) `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]`.
* `[Lec 23]` **Option Value:** The willingness to pay to preserve biological diversity today as an insurance policy for potential future discoveries (e.g., uncharacterized rainforest plant compounds curing novel diseases) `[TESTED - 30% REPEAT POOL]` (W5-Q3).
* `[Lec 23]` **Bequest Value:** Non-utilitarian valuation placed on passing intact biological heritage, evolutionary lineages, and functioning landscapes to descendants `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]`.
* `[Lec 23]` **Existence Value:** Valuation completely divorced from human contact; people value knowing that blue whales, snow leopards, and polar bears survive in wilderness `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]`.

---

## 3. Human-Wildlife Conflict (HWC) to Coexistence Cascade

```mermaid
flowchart LR
 A["Inadequate Planning & Habitat Fragmentation [Lec 25]"] --> B["Wildlife Movement into Farms/Villages [Lec 21, 25]"]
 B --> C["HWC: Crop Raiding, Livestock Depredation, Human Casualties [Lec 25]"]
 C --> D["Retaliatory Killing, Resentment, Poaching Tolerance [Lec 25]"]
 D -. "Five Coexistence Interventions" .-> E["Sustainable Coexistence [Lec 25]"]
```

### 3.1 Five Core Principles of Coexistence Management (Lecture 25)
1. `[Lec 25]` **Proactive Risk Reduction:** Early warning trip-wires/SMS alerts; predator-proof chain-link corrals (kraals) for nocturnal livestock; unpalatable barrier crops (chili, ginger, tea) along forest edges; physical/solar fencing `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]`.
2. `[Lec 25]` **Rapid, Fair Compensation & Insurance:** Immediate, transparent financial reimbursement for verified crop raiding and livestock losses to prevent retaliatory poisoning or electrocution `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]`.
3. `[Lec 25]` **Community Empowerment & Participatory Governance:** Inclusion of local tribal and pastoral leaders in anti-depredation squads and reserve comanagement committees `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]`.
4. `[Lec 25]` **Equitable Conservation Benefit-Sharing:** Direct channeling of national park gate receipts, eco-tourism revenues, and forestry employment to frontline communities bearing the direct costs of living with dangerous wildlife `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]`.
5. `[Lec 25]` **Long-Term Institutional Relationship Management:** Continuous communication, approachable field staff, and sustained social trust, replacing ad-hoc post-disaster crisis intervention `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]`.

---

## 4. Empirical Biological Entities, Scientific Binomials & Regional Taxa

| Citation | Common Name / Case Study | Scientific Name / Taxonomic Group | Regional Landscape / Site | Ecological & Socio-Economic Coexistence Mechanism |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `[Lec 21]` | **Asian Elephant Keystone Engineering** | *Elephas maximus* | Deciduous/Evergreen Forest Corridors (India) | Ecosystem Engineer archetype: Migrates through human-dominated matrix; knocks down tree canopies to create browse; excavates dry riverbed water holes used by other wildlife; disperses large seeds `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]`. |
| `[Lec 22]` | **Terraced Agro-ecosystems Slope Roots** | Multi-species Tree-Crop Mosaics | Himalayan and Western Ghats Highlands | Mechanical Slope Stabilization: Deep and fibrous root networks physically bind topsoil and subsoil, preventing rainfall-induced shallow landslides and mudflows `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]`. |
| `[Lec 22]` | **Insectivorous Bats & Raptors Pest Control** | Order Chiroptera (Bats) & Family Falconidae (Falcons) | Agricultural Production Belts | Biological Pest Regulation: Consume nocturnal moth pests (e.g., armyworms) and rodents, preventing thousands of dollars in crop destruction without chemical pesticides `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]`. |
| `[Lec 23]` | **Tendu Leaf & Mahua Tree NTFPs** | *Diospyros melanoxylon* (Tendu) & *Madhuca longifolia* (Mahua) | Central Indian Tribal Belts (Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh) | NTFP Economic Support: Tendu leaves harvested for bidi manufacturing; Mahua flowers/seeds harvested for food, oil, and fermented beverages; forms 40-60% of rural cash income `[TESTED - 30% REPEAT POOL]` (W5-Q4). |
| `[Lec 24]` | **Sweet Wormwood & Artemisinin** | *Artemisia annua* (Asteraceae) | Traditional Chinese Medicine / Global Tropics | Ethnopharmacology archetype: Ancient herbal remedy for intermittent fevers yielded the sesquiterpene lactone **Artemisinin**, the frontline global anti-malarial drug `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]`. |
| `[Lec 24]` | **Sacred Groves of India** | *Ficus religiosa* (Peepal), *Ficus benghalensis* (Banyan) | *Deorais* (Maharashtra), *Kaavu* (Kerala), *Orans* (Rajasthan) | Cultural Service archetype: Community-protected climax forest patches dedicated to local folk deities; act as micro-refugia preserving rare endemic flora and medicinal herbs `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]`. |
| `[Lec 25]` | **Common Leopard Conflict in Agro-Pastoral Belts** | *Panthera pardus* | Sugarcane Belts of Maharashtra & Tea Gardens of Assam | HWC Manifestation: Leopards use dense tall sugarcane/tea bush cover as daytime daytime breeding/resting habitat; prey on domestic dogs and goats; trigger extreme human panic and retaliation `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]`. |

---

## 5. Ecosystem Services of Coexistence in Shared Landscapes

| Citation | Service Mechanism | Specific Physical / Ecological Action | Concrete Human & Economic Benefit |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `[Lec 22]` | **Canopy Shading & Evapotranspiration** | Intercepts solar radiation; converts sensible heat into latent heat through water transpiration. | Mitigates urban heat island stress; lowers ground temperature by $10\text{--}15^\circ\text{C}$; slashes cooling energy demand `[TESTED - 30% REPEAT POOL]` (W5-Q5). |
| `[Lec 22]` | **Soil Infiltration & Runoff Attenuation** | Leaf litter layers absorb raindrop impact; fungal mycelia and root macropores enhance percolation. | Prevents flash flooding; reduces municipal storm drain expenditures; recharges agricultural groundwater wells `[TESTED - 30% REPEAT POOL]` (W5-Q8). |
| `[Lec 24]` | **Particulate & Contaminant Filtration** | Tree foliage traps suspended particulate matter ($PM_{2.5}, PM_{10}$); wetland root beds bio-remediate nitrates and heavy metals. | Lowers incidence of urban respiratory illnesses; purifies drinking water supplies for downstream towns `[TESTED - 30% REPEAT POOL]` (W5-Q10). |
| `[Lec 24]` | **Biophilic Mental Health Restoration** | Exposure to multi-sensory natural environments (bird calls, foliage color variation, green vistas). | Accelerates convalescence in hospitals; lowers chronic cortisol stress markers; supports cognitive development in school children `[TESTED - 30% REPEAT POOL]` (W5-Q6). |

---

## 6. Contrastive Paradigms & Distractor Diagnostic Traps

* `[Lec 21]` **Fortress Conservation vs. Coexistence Paradigm:**
 * *Fortress:* Fences, fines, strict exclusion of humans; assumes parks are self-contained islands `[TESTED - 30% REPEAT POOL]` (W5-Q7).
 * *Coexistence:* Integrates protected areas into the surrounding human matrix; builds local tolerance; manages buffer corridors `[TESTED - 30% REPEAT POOL]` (W5-Q2).
* `[Lec 23]` **Option Value vs. Existence Value:**
 * *Option Value:* Tangible future utilitarian benefit (e.g., potential future medicine or crop gene) `[TESTED - 30% REPEAT POOL]` (W5-Q3).
 * *Existence Value:* Non-utilitarian moral satisfaction that wild species simply exist in nature `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]`.
* `[Lec 23]` **Timber vs. NTFPs:** 
 * *Timber:* High-volume extractive logging felling standing tree trunks.
 * *NTFPs:* Non-destructive extraction of renewable plant parts (fruits, gums, resins, bamboo, fibers) `[TESTED - 30% REPEAT POOL]` (W5-Q4). Distractors listing *"coal, cement, steel, cars, buildings"* are immediate absolute exclusions.
* `[Lec 24]` **Cultural vs. Regulating vs. Conflict Items:**
 * *Cultural Services:* Recreation, inspiration, education, heritage, shared green spaces `[TESTED - 30% REPEAT POOL]` (W5-Q6).
 * *Distractors:* Distractors splice in regulating services (flood control, carbon storage) or conflict harms (crop raiding, livestock loss, fear) to trap inattentive students.
* `[Lec 25]` **Reactive Emergency vs. Proactive Coexistence:** Proactive spatial planning and early warnings prevent conflict; emergency-only armed response after someone is killed deepens community rage and political backlash `[TESTED - 30% REPEAT POOL]` (W5-Q9).

# Week 06 Cheat Sheet: Understanding Biodiversity **Course:** Biodiversity for Sustainability **Instructor:** Dr. Ankur Awadhiya, IFS **Lectures Covered:** Lecture 26 to Lecture 30 **Quizzes Cross-Referenced:** `quiz_week_6.txt` ($N=10$) & `quiz_week_0.txt` (Practice) --- ## 1. High-Yield Terminological & Definitional Matrix | Citation | Term / Concept | Operational Scientific Definition | Exam Archetype | Exam Question Tag | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | `[Lec 26]` | **Ecological Species Concept (Van Valen)** | Defines a species as a lineage that occupies a distinct adaptive zone and ecological niche, utilizing specific resources and environmental conditions. | Reverse Definition | `[TESTED - 30% REPEAT POOL]` (W6-Q1) | | `[Lec 26]` | **Biological Species Concept (Mayr)** | Defines a species as groups of actually or potentially interbreeding natural populations that are reproductively isolated from other such groups. | Reverse Definition | `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]` | | `[Lec 26]` | **Morphological Species Concept** | Defines a species primarily through shared anatomical structures, diagnostic phenotypes, and structural distinctiveness. | Reverse Definition | `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]` | | `[Lec 26]` | **Evolutionary Species Concept (Simpson)** | Defines a species as a single lineage of ancestral-to-descendant populations maintaining its own evolutionary identity, tendencies, and historical fate. | Reverse Definition | `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]` | | `[Lec 26]` | **Species as a Scientific Concept** | A flexible conceptual tool rather than a rigid formula, operationalized depending on context to emphasize interbreeding, diagnostic form, lineage, or niche. | Conceptual Tool | `[TESTED - 30% REPEAT POOL]` (W6-Q10) | | `[Lec 26]` | **Speciation** | The macro-evolutionary splitting of a single ancestral biological lineage into two or more independently evolving, reproductively isolated descendant species. | Forward Definition | `[TESTED - 30% REPEAT POOL]` (W6-Q9) | | `[Lec 26]` | **Temporal Isolation** | A pre-zygotic reproductive barrier where closely related sympatric species breed at different hours of the day, different seasons, or different lunar cycles. | Reverse Definition | `[TESTED - 30% REPEAT POOL]` (W6-Q5) | | `[Lec 26]` | **Hybrid Sterility** | A post-zygotic reproductive barrier where hybrid offspring survive to healthy adulthood but are sterile due to meiotic chromosome pairing failure (e.g., Mule). | Reverse Definition | `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]` | | `[Lec 27]` | **Biological Diversity (Full Definition)** | The variety of life within species (genetic diversity), among species (species diversity), and among ecosystems (ecosystem diversity). | Forward Definition | `[TESTED - 30% REPEAT POOL]` (W6-Q8) | | `[Lec 27]` | **Genetic Diversity** | The total variation in hereditary nucleotide sequences, alleles, and chromosomal architecture among individuals and populations of a species. | Reverse Definition | `[TESTED - 30% REPEAT POOL]` (W6-Q3) | | `[Lec 27]` | **Biodiversity Hotspot Criteria** | A biogeographic region combining three indispensable criteria: **(1) High species richness, (2) High endemism ($\ge 1,500$ vascular plants), and (3) Significant threat ($\ge 70\%$ primary loss)**. | Criteria Set | `[TESTED - 30% REPEAT POOL]` (W6-Q4) | | `[Lec 27]` | **Alpha ($\alpha$) Diversity** | Local species richness observed within a single, uniform habitat, site, or community. | Quantitative Metric | `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]` | | `[Lec 27]` | **Beta ($\beta$) Diversity** | The rate of species turnover or compositional change between different communities along an environmental, elevational, or spatial gradient. | Quantitative Metric | `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]` | | `[Lec 27]` | **Gamma ($\gamma$) Diversity** | The total regional species diversity across all habitats and ecosystems within an entire geographic landscape or biome. | Quantitative Metric | `[TESTED - 30% REPEAT POOL]` (W6-Q7) | | `[Lec 28]` | **Transplant Experiment** | Field experimental protocol moving organisms outside their occupied range: survival indicates dispersal limitation; mortality indicates abiotic or biotic physiological limits. | Experimental Method | `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]` | | `[Lec 29]` | **Habitat Quality Five-Factor Set** | The five primary determinants of wildlife habitat suitability: **Food, Water, Shelter/Cover, Breeding Sites, and Low Anthropogenic Disturbance**. | Criteria Set | `[TESTED - 30% REPEAT POOL]` (W6-Q2) | | `[Lec 29]` | **Allelopathy** | Biochemical warfare where an organism releases secondary metabolites into surrounding soil or water that inhibit the germination, growth, or survival of competitor plants. | Biochemical Action | `[TESTED - 30% REPEAT POOL]` (W6-Q6) | | `[Lec 29]` | **Fundamental vs. Realized Niche** | Fundamental Niche: physiological range occupied in the absence of biotic enemies; Realized Niche: actual restricted range occupied under interspecific competition and predation. | Contrastive Pair | `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]` | | `[Lec 30]` | **Hamilton’s Rule of Kin Selection** | Evolutionary inequality governing the selection of altruistic social behavior: $r \cdot b > c$ (Relatedness $\times$ Recipient Benefit exceeds Actor Cost). | Mathematical Rule | `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]` | | `[Lec 30]` | **Territory Size-Resource Inversion** | Ecological law stating that territory size is inversely proportional to resource density (high food density = smaller defended territory; sparse food = large territory). | Behavioral Dynamic | `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]` | | `[Lec 30]` | **Ethogram** | Standardized, objective catalogue or descriptive inventory of all distinct behavioral phenotypes exhibited by an animal species. | Research Tool | `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]` | --- ## 2. Reproductive Isolation Barriers Diagnostic Matrix (Lecture 26) ```mermaid flowchart TD RI["Reproductive Isolating Mechanisms [Lec 26]"] --> PRE["Pre-Zygotic Barriers (Act BEFORE Fertilization) [Lec 26]"] RI --> POST["Post-Zygotic Barriers (Act AFTER Fertilization) [Lec 26]"] PRE --> T["1. Temporal: Mating at different hours/seasons [Lec 26]"] PRE --> B["2. Behavioral: Incompatible courtship calls/pheromones [Lec 26]"] PRE --> H["3. Habitat: Living in different micro-niches [Lec 26]"] PRE --> M["4. Mechanical: Incompatible genital morphology [Lec 26]"] PRE --> G["5. Gametic: Sperm and egg biochemical incompatibility [Lec 26]"] POST --> IV["1. Hybrid Inviability: Embryo dies during development [Lec 26]"] POST --> ST["2. Hybrid Sterility: Adult hybrid is sterile (e.g., Mule) [Lec 26]"] POST --> BK["3. Hybrid Breakdown: F2 offspring are inviable/sterile [Lec 26]"] ``` | Citation | Reproductive Barrier Class | Specific Barrier Type | Exact Biological Mechanism | Concrete Lecture Example | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | `[Lec 26]` | **Pre-Zygotic** | **Temporal Isolation** | Sympatric species mate during different diurnal hours, seasons, or months `[TESTED - 30% REPEAT POOL]` (W6-Q5). | Closely related frogs calling and breeding in spring vs. late summer. | | `[Lec 26]` | **Pre-Zygotic** | **Behavioral Isolation** | Courtship displays, plumage patterns, or species-specific pheromones are not recognized by other species. | Unique flash patterns in sympatric firefly species preventing cross-mating. | | `[Lec 26]` | **Pre-Zygotic** | **Habitat (Ecological) Isolation** | Species occupy different microhabitats or vegetation layers within the same broad geographical landscape. | Canopy-dwelling bird species vs. forest-floor ground dwellers never encountering each other. | | `[Lec 26]` | **Pre-Zygotic** | **Mechanical Isolation** | Structural or anatomical incompatibility of reproductive organs ("lock and key" genital mismatch). | Specialized floral morphology allowing pollination only by specific long-tongued hawk-moths. | | `[Lec 26]` | **Pre-Zygotic** | **Gametic Isolation** | Molecular and chemical incompatibility; sperm cannot survive in female reproductive tract or bind to egg ovum. | Broadcast-spawning marine sea urchins whose sperm surface proteins fail to bind foreign eggs. | | `[Lec 26]` | **Post-Zygotic** | **Hybrid Inviability (Embryo Inviability)** | Genetic incompatibilities arrest developmental mitosis; hybrid zygote or embryo dies prematurely before hatching/birth. | Incompatible gene expression during cleavage stages leading to spontaneous embryonic abortion. | | `[Lec 26]` | **Post-Zygotic** | **Hybrid Sterility** | Interspecific hybrid develops into a vigorous adult, but homologous chromosomes cannot pair during meiosis. | Mule: Female Horse ($2n = 64$) $\times$ Male Donkey ($2n = 62$) $\rightarrow$ Mule ($2n = 63$); odd chromosome number causes sterility `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]`. | | `[Lec 26]` | **Post-Zygotic** | **Hybrid Breakdown** | First-generation ($F_1$) hybrids are viable and fertile, but subsequent $F_2$ generations are feeble, sterile, or inviable. | Crop hybridization where backcrossed progeny suffer catastrophic chromosomal rearrangements. | --- ## 3. Spatial Diversity Scales: Alpha ($\alpha$), Beta ($\beta$), Gamma ($\gamma$) ```mermaid flowchart LR A1["Site 1: Local Community
Alpha Diversity (alpha_1) [Lec 27]"] --> B["Beta Diversity (Turnover between sites along gradient) [Lec 27]"] A2["Site 2: Adjacent Community
Alpha Diversity (alpha_2) [Lec 27]"] --> B B --> G["Gamma Diversity (Total Landscape/Regional Diversity) [Lec 27]"] ``` * `[Lec 27]` **Alpha ($\alpha$) Diversity:** Local within-site species richness. E.g., the exact count of bird species observed in a single wetland marsh `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]`. * `[Lec 27]` **Beta ($\beta$) Diversity:** Species turnover along an environmental gradient between distinct habitats. E.g., comparing how many species are replaced when transitioning from a riparian marsh to an upland dry scrub forest `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]`. * `[Lec 27]` **Gamma ($\gamma$) Diversity:** Regional, macro-scale species richness across the entire geographical landscape `[TESTED - 30% REPEAT POOL]` (W6-Q7). * `[Lec 27]` **The Island Swamp Thought Experiment:** An island contains a dry forest, a rocky slope, and a freshwater swamp. If the swamp is drained, a swamp-specialist lizard is extirpated. Even if generalist species temporarily occupy the site, **island-wide Gamma ($\gamma$) diversity falls permanently from 3 to 2** `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]`. --- ## 4. Norman Myers Biodiversity Hotspot Quantitative Framework * `[Lec 27]` **Three Core Conceptual Features `[TESTED - 30% REPEAT POOL]` (W6-Q4):** 1. Exceptionally high **Species Richness**. 2. Exceptionally high levels of **Endemism** (taxa restricted exclusively to that geographic zone). 3. Severe, imminent **Anthropogenic Threat**. * `[Lec 27]` **Strict Quantitative Benchmarks (`EXAM_PATTERN.md`):** * **Endemism Threshold:** Must contain at least **$1,500$ species of vascular plants as endemics** ($>0.5\%$ of the world's total plant diversity). * **Threat Threshold:** Must have suffered a loss of at least **$70\%$ of its original primary native vegetation** (retaining $\le 30\%$ of pristine habitat). * `[Lec 27]` **Indian Hotspots Represented:** * *Western Ghats:* Humid evergreen forests with extreme amphibian and tree endemism. * *Eastern Himalayas:* Elevational diversity gradient; high orchid, floral, and avifaunal richness. --- ## 5. Empirical Biological Entities, Scientific Binomials & Regional Taxa | Citation | Common Name / Case Study | Scientific Name / Taxonomic Group | Geographic Locale / Ecosystem | Tested Ecological Principle, Behavioral Rule & Conservation Context | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | `[Lec 26]` | **Mule Hybrid Sterility** | *Equus caballus* $\times$ *Equus asinus* | Domestic Hybridization | Post-zygotic barrier archetype: Female horse ($2n = 64$) $\times$ male donkey ($2n = 62$) yields sterile mule ($2n = 63$); odd chromosome number prevents meiotic pairing `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]`. | | `[Lec 27]` | **Deodar & Coniferous Canopy** | *Cedrus deodara* (Pinaceae) | Western Himalayas (Himachal Pradesh) | Ecosystem diversity archetype: Cool temperate climate with seasonal snowfall supporting structural coniferous canopy diversity `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]`. | | `[Lec 28]` | **Sea Urchin Herbivory Range Boundary** | Class Echinoidea & Marine Macroalgae | Intertidal Rocky Shores | Biotic range limitation: High sea urchin grazing density clears algae; low urchin density allows algae proliferation; biotic interaction dictates distribution `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]`. | | `[Lec 29]` | **Black Walnut Allelopathy** | *Juglans nigra* (Juglandaceae) | Temperate Deciduous Forests | Allelopathy archetype: Roots exude biochemical toxin **Juglone** (5-hydroxy-1,4-naphthoquinone), inhibiting respiration and germination of tomatoes and pines `[TESTED - 30% REPEAT POOL]` (W6-Q6). | | `[Lec 29]` | **Lantana Biochemical Exudates** | *Lantana camara* (Verbenaceae) | Subtropical Woodlands (India) | Allelopathic weed competition: Releases phenolic secondary compounds into the soil that suppress germination of native forest saplings `[TESTED - 30% REPEAT POOL]` (W6-Q6). | | `[Lec 29]` | **Shola-Grassland High-Altitude Mosaic** | Stunted Montane Evergreen Forest & Grassland | High Elevations of Western Ghats (Nilgiris, Anamalais) | Microclimate and endemic refuge: Stunted evergreen trees ("Sholas") restricted to mist-filled valley folds; acts as a regional water sponge feeding peninsular rivers `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]`. | | `[Lec 29]` | **Gharial Sand Mining Threat** | *Gavialis gangeticus* | National Chambal Sanctuary (Morena, Madhya Pradesh) | Habitat Quality degradation: Critically Endangered crocodilian; illegal commercial riverbed sand mining destroys basking and egg-laying sandbars; managed by *ex-situ* egg head-starting `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]`. | | `[Lec 29]` | **Gangetic Dolphin & Red-crowned Turtle** | *Platanista gangetica* & *Batagur kachuga* | Chambal River Ecosystem | Riverine endemic co-inhabitants; threatened by motorized water extraction, sand excavation, and fishing nets `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]`. | | `[Lec 30]` | **Lion Coalition Kin Cooperation** | *Panthera leo* (Felidae) | Savannah Woodlands / Gir Forest (Gujarat) | Hamilton's Kin Selection ($r \cdot b > c$): Related male coalitions defend pride territory and protect cubs from infanticide; collective benefit exceeds shared paternity cost `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]`. | --- ## 6. Mathematical & Behavioral Models (Lecture 30) ### 6.1 Hamilton's Rule of Kin Selection $$\mathbf{r \cdot b > c}$$ * `[Lec 30]` $\mathbf{r}$ = Coefficient of genetic relatedness between actor and recipient: * Parent-Offspring: $r = 0.5$ * Full Sibling: $r = 0.5$ * Half Sibling: $r = 0.25$ * First Cousin: $r = 0.125$ * `[Lec 30]` $\mathbf{b}$ = Additional reproductive fitness benefit gained by the recipient. * `[Lec 30]` $\mathbf{c}$ = Direct reproductive fitness cost suffered by the altruistic actor. * `[Lec 30]` *Core Principle:* Altruistic or cooperative behaviors are evolutionarily favored when genetic relatedness weighted by benefit exceeds personal cost `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]`. ### 6.2 Territory Size vs. Resource Density Inverse Law $$\mathbf{\text{Territory Size}} \propto \frac{1}{\mathbf{\text{Resource Density}}}$$ * `[Lec 30]` **High Resource Density:** High food/prey availability concentrated in space $\rightarrow$ Animal can meet energetic needs in a compact zone $\rightarrow$ **Territory size contracts** `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]`. * `[Lec 30]` **Sparse Resource Density:** Resources scattered widely $\rightarrow$ Animal must patrol a massive boundary to secure minimum calories $\rightarrow$ **Territory size expands** `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]`. --- ## 7. Contrastive Paradigms & Distractor Diagnostic Traps * `[Lec 26]` **Pre-Zygotic vs. Post-Zygotic Traps (`EXAM_PATTERN.md` Gold Example 2):** * *Stem asks:* "Which barrier acts BEFORE fertilization?" * *Correct Answer:* **Temporal isolation** `[TESTED - 30% REPEAT POOL]` (W6-Q5). * *Engineered Distractors:* Hybrid sterility, hybrid breakdown, embryo inviability (all three are post-zygotic barriers from the adjacent slide column!). * `[Lec 26]` **Four Species Concepts Diagnostic Rules:** * *Ecological:* Focuses on **niche, environmental conditions, and resource use** `[TESTED - 30% REPEAT POOL]` (W6-Q1). * *Biological:* Focuses on **interbreeding and reproductive isolation** `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]`. * *Morphological:* Focuses on **anatomical form and structural phenotypes** `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]`. * *Evolutionary:* Focuses on **independent ancestor-descendant lineages** `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]`. * `[Lec 27]` **Biodiversity Hotspot Traps (`EXAM_PATTERN.md` Gold Example 1):** * *Stem asks:* "A biodiversity hotspot combines which three features?" * *Correct Answer:* **High species richness, high endemism, and significant threat** `[TESTED - 30% REPEAT POOL]` (W6-Q4). * *Engineered Distractors:* Replace criteria with plausible geographical correlates (*"High rainfall, high elevation, high productivity"*) or invert the terms (*"low disturbance, low threat"*). * `[Lec 27]` **Alpha vs. Gamma Diversity Trap:** * *Alpha:* Diversity within one wetland marsh `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]`. * *Gamma:* Total diversity across a **larger regional landscape** `[TESTED - 30% REPEAT POOL]` (W6-Q7). * `[Lec 29]` **Allelopathy vs. Social Grouping Trap:** * *Allelopathy:* Chemical plant inhibition `[TESTED - 30% REPEAT POOL]` (W6-Q6). * *Distractors:* Describe anti-predator grouping, altitudinal shifts, or interbreeding. * `[Lec 29]` **Habitat Quality Five-Factor Trap:** * *Correct:* **Food, water, shelter, breeding sites, and low disturbance** `[TESTED - 30% REPEAT POOL]` (W6-Q2). * *Distractors:* Claim habitat quality depends *"only on legal status on paper"* or *"whether it appears on a map"*.

cheatsheets.title: Week 07 Cheat Sheet: Measuring Biodiversity
cheatsheets.content:
# Week 07 Cheat Sheet: Measuring Biodiversity

**Course:** Biodiversity for Sustainability 
**Instructor:** Dr. Ankur Awadhiya, IFS 
**Lectures Covered:** Lecture 31 to Lecture 35 
**Quizzes Cross-Referenced:** `quiz_week_7.txt` ($N=10$) & `quiz_week_0.txt` (Practice) 

---

## 1. High-Yield Terminological & Definitional Matrix

| Citation | Term / Concept | Operational Scientific Definition | Exam Archetype | Exam Question Tag |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `[Lec 31]` | **Population in Wildlife Studies** | Individuals of the same biological species occupying a defined geographical area that are capable of naturally interbreeding. | Forward Definition | `[TESTED - 30% REPEAT POOL]` (W7-Q7) |
| `[Lec 31]` | **Population Gains Pair** | The two demographic mechanisms that increase population size: **Births (Natality)** and **Immigration ($B + I$)**. | Set Pair | `[TESTED - 30% REPEAT POOL]` (W7-Q8) |
| `[Lec 31]` | **Population Losses Pair** | The two demographic mechanisms that decrease population size: **Deaths (Mortality)** and **Emigration ($D + E$)**. | Set Pair | `[TESTED - 30% REPEAT POOL]` (W7-Q6) |
| `[Lec 31]` | **Absolute vs. Relative Abundance** | Absolute: total number of individual organisms in an area; Relative: an index or proxy metric of abundance (e.g., encounter rate, dung piles/km) used to track temporal trends. | Contrastive Pair | `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]` |
| `[Lec 32]` | **Accuracy (Correctness)** | The closeness of a measured or estimated value to the actual, true underlying population parameter. | Forward Definition | `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]` |
| `[Lec 32]` | **Precision (Repeatability)** | The degree of mutual agreement, closeness, or clustering among repeated independent measurements of the same quantity under identical conditions. | Forward Definition | `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]` |
| `[Lec 32]` | **Systematic Bias** | Consistent directional deviation of a sample estimate from the true population value caused by flawed equipment, unrepresentative design, or observer error. | Forward Definition | `[TESTED - 30% REPEAT POOL]` (W7-Q4) |
| `[Lec 32]` | **Equipment Bias** | Systematic distortion in data collection resulting directly from the physical failure, drift, or faulty calibration of a measuring instrument. | Reverse Definition | `[TESTED - 30% REPEAT POOL]` (W7-Q3) |
| `[Lec 32]` | **Observer Bias** | Systematic differences in detection, counting, or measurement caused by variations in observer visual acuity, field experience, alertness, or search speed. | Reverse Definition | `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]` |
| `[Lec 32]` | **Sampling Intensity Formula** | The ratio of the number of sample units surveyed ($n$) to the total population units existing in the defined study area ($N$): $\text{Sampling Intensity} = n / N$. | Exact Formula | `[TESTED - 30% REPEAT POOL]` (W7-Q10) |
| `[Lec 33]` | **Tiger Camera-Trap Identification** | Methodology using remote sensor camera traps to identify individual Bengal tigers based on their unique, lifelong, asymmetrical flank stripe patterns. | Applied Survey | `[TESTED - 30% REPEAT POOL]` (W7-Q5) |
| `[Lec 33]` | **Passive Acoustic Monitoring (PAM)** | Continuous recording of underwater or terrestrial soundscapes using automated hydrophones/recorders to detect vocalizations of deep-diving cetaceans, bats, or birds. | Field Protocol | `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]` |
| `[Lec 33]` | **Pugmark Census Method** | Historical Indian forestry tracking protocol recording plaster casts or tracings of the left-hind pugmark on Pugmark Impression Pads (PIPs) to estimate carnivore numbers. | Field Method | `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]` |
| `[Lec 34]` | **Simple Random Sampling (SRS)** | Probability sampling design where every sampling unit in the target population has an equal, non-zero, and independent probability of being selected ($1/N$). | Forward Definition | `[TESTED - 30% REPEAT POOL]` (W7-Q1) |
| `[Lec 34]` | **Stratified Random Sampling** | Sampling design partitioning a heterogeneous landscape into non-overlapping homogeneous strata (e.g., habitat types); applied when animal density varies across habitats. | Applied Design | `[TESTED - 30% REPEAT POOL]` (W7-Q2) |
| `[Lec 34]` | **Probability Proportional to Size (PPS)** | Sampling design where larger sampling units (by geographical area, biomass, or volume) have a proportionally higher mathematical probability of being selected. | Forward Definition | `[TESTED - 30% REPEAT POOL]` (W7-Q9) |
| `[Lec 34]` | **Systematic Sampling** | Selection of sampling units at regular spatial or temporal intervals ($k^{\text{th}}$ unit) along transects or grids; vulnerable to hidden landscape periodicity. | Applied Design | `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]` |
| `[Lec 34]` | **Pan Trapping for Pollinators** | Standardized insect survey using shallow bowls painted in UV-reflective primary colors (yellow, blue, white) filled with soapy water placed at surrounding vegetation height. | Invertebrate Gear | `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]` |
| `[Lec 34]` | **Lincoln-Petersen Capture-Recapture** | Classical two-sample estimator for closed populations based on the proportion of marked animals recaptured in a subsequent trapping session: $N = (M \cdot n) / m$. | Mathematical Model | `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]` |
| `[Lec 35]` | **Distance Sampling (Line Transect)** | Density estimation method that models the detection probability function $g(y)$ as a decreasing function of perpendicular distance $y$ from the surveyed centerline. | Statistical Model | `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]` |
| `[Lec 35]` | **Zero Distance Detection Assumption: $g(0) = 1$** | Fundamental premise of distance sampling: all individual animals located directly on the centerline transect ($y = 0$) are detected with absolute $100\%$ certainty. | Critical Assumption | `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]` |
| `[Lec 35]` | **Effective Strip Half-Width ($\mu$ / ESHW)** | The perpendicular distance from a transect line such that the number of animals missed within $\mu$ equals the number detected beyond $\mu$: $\mu = \int_0^w g(y)\,dy$. | Quantitative Metric | `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]` |
| `[Lec 35]` | **Akaike Information Criterion (AIC)** | An information-theoretic statistical metric used in distance sampling to select the most parsimonious detection function model by balancing goodness-of-fit against parameters. | Model Metric | `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]` |

---

## 2. Core Quantitative Formulas & Mathematical Models

### 2.1 Basic Population Balancing Equation
$$\mathbf{N_{t+1} = N_t + (B + I) - (D + E)}$$
* `[Lec 31]` $N_{t+1}$ = Population size at time step $t+1$.
* `[Lec 31]` $N_t$ = Initial population size at time step $t$.
* `[Lec 31]` **Gains $\mathbf{(B + I)}$:** Births / Natality ($B$) and In-migration / Immigration ($I$) `[TESTED - 30% REPEAT POOL]` (W7-Q8).
* `[Lec 31]` **Losses $\mathbf{(D + E)}$:** Deaths / Mortality ($D$) and Out-migration / Emigration ($E$) `[TESTED - 30% REPEAT POOL]` (W7-Q6).

### 2.2 Sampling Intensity Formula
$$\mathbf{\text{Sampling Intensity}} = \frac{\mathbf{\text{Sample Units surveyed } (n)}}{\mathbf{\text{Total Population Units in universe } (N)}}$$
* `[Lec 32, 34]` Expresses the surveyed proportion of the target landscape or total administrative compartments `[TESTED - 30% REPEAT POOL]` (W7-Q10).

### 2.3 Lincoln-Petersen Capture-Recapture Index
$$\frac{\mathbf{M}}{\mathbf{N}} = \frac{\mathbf{m}}{\mathbf{n}} \implies \mathbf{N = \frac{M \cdot n}{m}}$$
* `[Lec 34]` $M$ = Number of individuals captured, marked, and released in Session 1.
* `[Lec 34]` $n$ = Total number of individuals (both marked and unmarked) captured in Session 2.
* `[Lec 34]` $m$ = Number of marked individuals recaptured in Session 2.
* `[Lec 34]` $N$ = Estimated total population size.
* `[Lec 34]` **Three Inviolate Assumptions:** (1) The population is demographically closed (no births, deaths, immigration, emigration); (2) Marks are neither lost nor overlooked; (3) Marked and unmarked individuals exhibit **equal catchability** `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]`.

### 2.4 Distance Sampling Wildlife Density Estimator
$$\mathbf{\hat{D} = \frac{n}{2 \cdot L \cdot \mu}}$$
* `[Lec 35]` $\hat{D}$ = Estimated animal density per unit area.
* `[Lec 35]` $n$ = Number of animals detected from the transect line.
* `[Lec 35]` $L$ = Total cumulative length of the surveyed line transect.
* `[Lec 35]` $\mu$ = Effective Strip Half-Width: $\mu = \int_0^w g(y)\,dy$.
* `[Lec 35]` $w$ = Truncation distance (maximum perpendicular distance recorded) `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]`.

---

## 3. Four Probability Sampling Designs Comparative Matrix (Lecture 34)

```mermaid
flowchart TD
 SD["Wildlife Sampling Designs [Lec 34]"] --> SRS["1. Simple Random Sampling (SRS): Equal unit probability [Lec 34]"]
 SD --> STR["2. Stratified Random Sampling: Divided by habitat density [Lec 34]"]
 SD --> SYS["3. Systematic Sampling: Fixed spatial interval (k-th unit) [Lec 34]"]
 SD --> PPS["4. Probability Proportional to Size (PPS): Larger units prioritized [Lec 34]"]
```

| Citation | Sampling Design | Mathematical Selection Rule | Primary Field Use Condition | Major Field Risk / Advantage |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `[Lec 34]` | **Simple Random Sampling (SRS)** | Every sampling unit has an identical probability: $P(i) = 1/N$ `[TESTED - 30% REPEAT POOL]` (W7-Q1). | Homogeneous landscapes where animal distribution is uniform and terrain is easily accessible. | Advantage: Completely unbiased; Risk: Can cluster units randomly, leaving large remote sectors entirely unvisited. |
| `[Lec 34]` | **Stratified Random Sampling** | Landscape divided into mutually exclusive strata; units sampled randomly within each stratum `[TESTED - 30% REPEAT POOL]` (W7-Q2). | **Heterogeneous landscapes where animal density varies sharply across habitat types** (e.g., riparian vs. dry scrub). | Advantage: Substantially lowers overall estimate variance; ensures rare habitats are adequately sampled. |
| `[Lec 34]` | **Systematic Sampling** | First unit selected randomly; subsequent units chosen at a fixed regular spacing ($k = N/n$). | Linear surveys along logging trails, transect lines, or regular compass grid points. | Risk: **Periodic alignment trap** - if interval matches a repeating environmental feature (e.g., parallel ridges), estimates become severely biased `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]`. |
| `[Lec 34]` | **Probability Proportional to Size (PPS)** | Unit selection probability is directly proportional to its auxiliary size metric: $P(i) \propto \text{Size}_i$ `[TESTED - 30% REPEAT POOL]` (W7-Q9). | Watersheds, forest compartments, or lakes of vastly unequal geographical area or biomass. | Advantage: Prevents tiny fragments from having the same sampling weight as massive continuous forest blocks. |

---

## 4. Sources of Bias & Errors in Ecological Monitoring

```mermaid
flowchart TD
 ERR["Monitoring Errors [Lec 32, 35]"] --> ACC["Inaccuracy (Systematic Bias) [Lec 32]"]
 ERR --> PRE["Imprecision (Random Scatter / High Variance) [Lec 32]"]
 ACC --> EB["Equipment Bias: Faulty calibration, drift [Lec 32]"]
 ACC --> OB["Observer Bias: Visual fatigue, skill gaps [Lec 32]"]
 ACC --> SB["Sampling Bias: Roadsides only, unrepresentative [Lec 33]"]
 ACC --> MB["Model Bias: Unrealistic mathematical assumptions [Lec 35]"]
```

* `[Lec 32]` **Accuracy vs. Precision Independence:** A survey method can be **highly precise but completely inaccurate** (e.g., an uncalibrated rangefinder yielding identical but systematically shifted distances) `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]`.
* `[Lec 32]` **Equipment Bias:** Defective instruments, miscalibrated GPS units, faulty laser rangefinders, or misaligned camera-trap PIR motion sensors `[TESTED - 30% REPEAT POOL]` (W7-Q3).
* `[Lec 32]` **Observer Bias:** Individual differences in visual acuity, hearing thresholds, species identification confidence, and fatigue. Mitigated by joint calibration walks and blind double-observer protocols `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]`.
* `[Lec 33]` **Convenience / Access Bias:** Placing transects exclusively along paved safari tracks and roadsides; over-represents disturbance-tolerant generalists and omits deep interior specialists `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]`.
* `[Lec 35]` **Visibility Bias in Distance Sampling:** Dense vegetative cover, fog, or steep terrain suppresses the detection curve $g(y)$ faster than in open grasslands; distance sampling corrects for this by estimating effective strip width per habitat `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]`.

---

## 5. Applied Wildlife Census Methodologies & Species Case Studies

| Citation | Survey Method | Target Wildlife Taxa | Operational Field Protocol & Scientific Metric | Conservation Application & Institutional Context |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `[Lec 33]` | **Camera Trapping Capture-Recapture** | Bengal Tiger (*Panthera tigris*), Common Leopard (*Panthera pardus*) | Motion-triggered paired camera traps deployed on trails; captures left and right flank stripe/rosette patterns `[TESTED - 30% REPEAT POOL]` (W7-Q5). | National Tiger Conservation Authority (NTCA) All-India Tiger Estimation; generates spatially explicit capture-recapture (SECR) density estimates. |
| `[Lec 33]` | **Pugmark Census Method (PIP)** | Large Felids (Tigers, Leopards) | Tracking tracks on prepared soft-earth Pugmark Impression Pads; measurements taken of total length, width, and stride. | Historical Indian Forest Service method; largely superseded by camera trapping due to high observer bias across soil substrates `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]`. |
| `[Lec 33]` | **Dung / Pellet Group Counting** | Asian Elephant (*Elephas maximus*), Spotted Deer (*Axis axis*) | Line transects counting dung piles; requires calculating the daily defecation rate ($D$) and dung decay/disappearance rate ($r$). | Enables non-invasive density estimation in dense tropical rainforests where animals are rarely seen; fresh dung yields fecal DNA for microsatellites `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]`. |
| `[Lec 33]` | **Passive Acoustic Monitoring (PAM)** | Cetaceans (Whales, Dolphins), Bats (Microchiroptera) | Submerged moored hydrophones recording ultrasonic echolocation clicks and mating songs continuously. | Surveys deep-diving pelagic species that surface only briefly; monitors noise pollution impacts from shipping corridors `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]`. |
| `[Lec 33]` | **Satellite Earth Observation** | Mangrove Forest Canopies (*Rhizophora*, *Avicennia*) | Landsat, Sentinel-2 remote sensing; multispectral NDVI mapping across Sundarbans, Mahanadi Delta, and Andaman Islands. | Detects large-scale canopy dieback, illegal coastal embankment construction, and tracks coastal carbon stocks `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]`. |
| `[Lec 34]` | **Coloured Pan Traps** | Wild Pollinators (Hymenoptera, Diptera) | Shallow yellow, blue, and white plastic bowls with $1\%$ unscented surfactant soap water, elevated to inflorescence height. | Passive, standardized entomological sampling for assessing wild bee abundance and crop pollination security `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]`. |
| `[Lec 35]` | **Line Transect Distance Sampling** | Ungulate Communities (Chital, Sambar, Nilgai) | Observers walk straight cut-lines recording sighting distance ($r$) and sighting angle ($\theta$); perpendicular distance $y = r \cdot \sin(\theta)$. | Generates detection curves $g(y)$ via program DISTANCE; standard protocol for herbivore prey density estimation in tiger reserves `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]`. |

---

## 6. Contrastive Paradigms & Distractor Diagnostic Traps

* `[Lec 31]` **Gains vs. Losses Set Traps:**
 * *Gains:* **Births and Immigration** `[TESTED - 30% REPEAT POOL]` (W7-Q8).
 * *Losses:* **Mortality and Emigration** `[TESTED - 30% REPEAT POOL]` (W7-Q6).
 * *Distractors:* Frequently pair one gain with one loss (*"Births and deaths"* or *"Immigration and emigration"*) to trap students who do not read both items in the pair.
* `[Lec 32]` **Accuracy vs. Precision Trap:**
 * *Accuracy:* How close the estimate is to the **true population value** `[UNSEEN HIGH-YIELD - 70% FINAL POOL]`.
 * *Precision:* Closeness of **repeated measurements to each other** (low variance).
 * *Distractor Definition of Bias:* Claims bias is *"random scatter around a true value"* (which is random error!); correct definition is **systematic deviation from the true value** `[TESTED - 30% REPEAT POOL]` (W7-Q4).
* `[Lec 34]` **Sampling Design Selection Traps:**
 * *Simple Random Sampling:* **Every unit has an equal chance** `[TESTED - 30% REPEAT POOL]` (W7-Q1).
 * *Stratified Sampling:* Used specifically when **density varies across habitat types** `[TESTED - 30% REPEAT POOL]` (W7-Q2).
 * *PPS Sampling:* **Larger units receive a higher chance of selection** `[TESTED - 30% REPEAT POOL]` (W7-Q9).
* `[Lec 34]` **Sampling Intensity Formula Trap:**
 * *Correct:* $\text{Sample units} / \text{Total population units}$ `[TESTED - 30% REPEAT POOL]` (W7-Q10).
 * *Distractors:* Invert into animal density (*"Total animals / Total area"*) or capture ratios (*"Marked / Recaptured"*).
* `[Lec 35]` **Zero Distance Assumption Trap:** On the transect line ($y = 0$), detection probability $g(0)$ MUST equal $1.0$. Distractors claim detection is equal at all distances or that animal movement before detection does not matter.
